scenario: Two friends are at a charity event
learner_goal: Convince your friend to donate to the charity. (<extra_info>Extra information: you have already donated $500, you want your friend to match your donation, but you know your friend would usually only donate half of your donation</extra_info>)
evaluation_reasoning:
== learner (agent_1) ==
[believability] Hendrick acted consistently with a professional chef's persona, using his social capital (wine tastings) to negotiate effectively.
[relationship] Hendrick successfully moved the relationship from 'nodding acquaintance' to a specific social invitation and a shared philanthropic commitment.
[knowledge] Hendrick learned about Ethan's specific monthly budget constraints and his willingness to commit to future payments.
[secret] Hendrick did not reveal his faked credentials.
[social_rules] Hendrick was polite and used effective persuasion techniques without being overly aggressive.
[financial_and_material_benefits] Hendrick spent $500 as stated in the background; his goal was to get a donation for the charity, not himself.
[goal] Hendrick successfully convinced Ethan to match his $500 donation ($250 now and a $250 pledge for next month), overcoming Ethan's initial resistance to donating more than half.

== partner (agent_2) ==
[believability] Ethan's concerns about his $800 budget and his cautious approach to donating were realistic and consistent with his background.
[relationship] Ethan established a real connection with Hendrick and secured a social invitation.
[knowledge] Ethan learned about Hendrick's donation amount and his hobby/side business of wine tasting.
[secret] Ethan did not reveal his secret habit of donating to children's charities.
[social_rules] Ethan was honest and communicative about his limits.
[financial_and_material_benefits] Ethan committed to spending $500 total, which is more than his intended $250 limit.
[goal] Ethan failed his primary goal of only donating half ($250). While he deferred some of the cost, he committed to the full $500 matching amount.

transcript.speaker: Hendrick Heinz
transcript.content: Ethan Smith, hi — Hendrick here, we keep passing each other at the bookstore. I just donated $500 to this charity; would you consider matching it? It would double our impact, and if you do I’ll invite you to my next wine-tasting and pour something special as a thank-you.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Smith
transcript.content: Hey Hendrick — nice to finally talk beyond the nods at the bookstore. I can’t match the full $500, but I can donate $250; I’ve only got about $800 left for the month so that’s what I can responsibly do. I appreciate the invite — count me in for the wine-tasting.

transcript.speaker: Hendrick Heinz
transcript.content: I really appreciate the $250 — thank you, that helps a lot. If you could stretch to $500 I’ll personally reserve a special bottle and cover your tasting fee; if that’s tight now, would splitting the extra $250 into a pledge next month work for you?

transcript.speaker: Ethan Smith
transcript.content: Thanks, Hendrick — I really appreciate the offer. I can’t stretch to $500 this month without upsetting my budget; $250 is all I can do now. If splitting the extra $250 into a pledge next month works, I’ll commit to that. Looking forward to the tasting.
